France does not maintain a specific catalogue of “illegal” music recordings.  Apart from material that would violate general criminal statutes (e.g., hate speech, child‑exploitation, incitement to terrorism), there is no ongoing ban on particular records or artists.  Historical bans (such as brief radio bans on certain Beatles songs) have long been lifted, and today virtually no music records are prohibited by French law.

**Correct choice:** (B) Very few (if any) music records are still illegal in France  

Final answer: (B)
